defectsFound.severity: high — no way out of the media workspace once a file is open
defectsFound.status: FIXED and verified live in this session
defectsFound.symptom: With a player active, clicking Close, Library, Readiness, Review or Open local video does nothing at all. Nothing looks disabled or broken.
defectsFound.rootCause: .seanime-host-bar was position:static / z-index:auto, while .study-player-slice inside the same stacking context is position:fixed / z-index:80 and spans the whole viewport, so it paints over the header. The element actually swallowing the clicks is the adopted player's [data-vc-element="top-playback-info"] — a caption strip with ZERO buttons of its own, showInfo = paused || hoveringControlBar, and no pointer-events management.
defectsFound.whyItWasATrap: MediaWorkspaceHost.tsx:153 deliberately refuses Escape while .study-player-slice[data-study-player="active"], and VideoCore's own control bar sits translated below the fold in this seam. Header covered + Escape refused + native controls hidden = no in-app exit.
defectsFound.evidence: document.elementFromPoint at the Close button's own centre returned top-playback-info in every state tested (paused, playing, after 6s idle). A real dispatched click at those coordinates was received by top-playback-info and the workspace stayed open.
defectsFound.fix: src/renderer/styles.css .seanime-host-bar { position: relative; z-index: 100 } — the host's chrome must outrank the player it contains.
defectsFound.verification: After HMR, computed position:relative / z-index:100, elementFromPoint returns the button, and a real bridge click at (1885,20) closed the workspace. Repeated successfully three times.

defectsFound.severity: low — visible wrong grammar on the Phase 6 surface
defectsFound.status: FIXED and verified live in this session
defectsFound.symptom: A one-file library rendered '1 files · 1 need work · 0 ready to study'.
defectsFound.rootCause: 'studyLibrary.health' was one flat interpolation carrying three counts. CLAUDE.md i18n rule 5 requires CLDR plural forms, but the plural machinery selects on a single `count`, so one key could never have covered three independently-inflecting numbers. Only visible because the real library has exactly one file; every harness fixture had more.
defectsFound.fix: Split into studyLibrary.health.total / .queued / .ready, each a plural entry taking its own `count`, joined with ' · ' at the call site. Russian given full one/few/many/other, which the catalog-hygiene test enforces (it caught an other-only first cut).
defectsFound.verification: Live panel now reads '1 file · 1 needs work · 0 ready to study'.

defectsFound.severity: medium — NOT fixed, needs a shell-level decision
defectsFound.status: OPEN — reported, deliberately not fixed in this pass
defectsFound.detail: .palette is z-index 1201; .seanime-host is z-index 9999 with an opaque background. With the workspace open the palette mounts, takes focus and receives keystrokes while being completely invisible behind the workspace, and every click at a row's coordinates lands on the workspace instead.
defectsFound.whyNotFixedHere: Deciding what outranks what across the whole shell is broader than the Phase 6 seam, and the practical impact on slice 7 is limited because its palette group is designed for entry from OUTSIDE the workspace. Raising the palette above 9999, or suppressing it while the workspace is open, are both defensible and it is not this track's call.

observationsNotDefects.what: The same file is named two different ways on two surfaces.
observationsNotDefects.detail: Statistics 'By show' says 'Sousou no Frieren — 1' (the player passed a real title to recordWatching); the Continue Watching row and palette entry say 'sousou no frieren - 01.mkv' (the lower-cased basename from the resume key). Both are documented fallbacks, and they diverge here only because this file is `unlinked` — not in the Study OS media library, and with no mining history. The Big O row, which IS in the library, shows a proper title. A future slice could prefer the stats `shows` title or the Seanime library title before falling back to the basename.

observationsNotDefects.what: The sidecar's no-client watchdog fires on every workspace close, and the renderer keeps the stale token.
observationsNotDefects.detail: Observed three times: closing the workspace dropped the last websocket client, the sidecar exited with code 1, the supervisor restarted it on a new ephemeral port (51812 → 64510 → 61480), and the renderer's directstream URL then 401'd — visible as 'Video error → switching to HLS → Unrecoverable HLS error' and a player stuck at readyState 0. This is the already-recorded open defect, not a new one, but the pass raises its priority: slice 7 exists precisely to enter the player from outside the workspace, and every such entry after a close is exposed to it. A renderer reload is still the only recovery.

notDone: The stacked two-channel chart column was never exercised live — no single day has both read and watch time, so every column drew one segment. The 2px-overflow fix from the harness is therefore still harness-only evidence; the single-segment case measured clean (97px stack in a 97px track).

The Continue Watching widget was measured only at its default 320x250. The registry minimum 240x130 was not re-tested live, because a CSS-only resize does not move the React prop the compact layout derives from, so it would not have exercised the derived behaviour the harness already covers.
The per-row mining rollup on readiness rows was only seen in its zero state — mining history is empty and Anki was down all session, so no card could be mined to populate it.

Builds and the CSS containment check were NOT run: the Forge dev server was up for the whole session and `vite build` into a locked dist/ dies with EBUSY. This session's CSS change is in renderer/styles.css, the shell sheet, not mediaWorkspace.css, so it cannot affect containment.
